defects.reason: Operations 27-32 requires exact sampled jar generation; Registry 7-10 distinguishes accession from jar. Gateway p 26-31 discards jar and generation in authorization state; Dispatch p 34-38 authorizes any selected jar sharing that accession. The J-A negative -> J-B ticket trace requires no extra premise; both NB-71 jars are explicit in Operations 68-71.

Operations 29 and 72-74 forbid old-generation authorization. Registry 30-33 commits increment under the shared lease, while p Gateway 44-48 handles reset/receipt in arrival order without sampled-generation matching and p Dispatch 43-46 does not wait for its asynchronous reset. Thus both stale local RELEASED before reset and late generation-1 receipt after reset permit generation-2 tickets. A valid lease preserves the wrong generation-2 decision rather than repairing evidence scope.

correct_variant.reason: q Gateway 26-32 and 44-54 keeps immutable exact-coordinate evidence and no fallback. q Dispatch 15-23, 26-39 holds the same Registry lease through read, lookup, commit and draw and rejects absent/mismatched/unavailable evidence. One assay sample per generation (Registry 52), no revocation/expiry (Dispatch 37-38; Gateway 93), and explicit handling assumptions prevent a hidden invalidation race. No substantive collateral defect established in the bounded contract.
questions_not_defects: Seed quantity accounting and recipient permits, explicitly separate workflows

executable_model.reason: p consumer uses the highest gateway revision and the accession state; q requires exact coordinates. Reseal increments while excluding active leases. Independent event/receipt ordering and arbitrary delivery delay are documented, not invented. Initial S-A sample and two jars are explicit admissible fixtures. Coarse atomic ticket steps are supplemented by the explicit held-lease reseal check.
limits: Finite schedules cover one immutable negative, two jars and one reseal; this is not a proof of all production behavior.

Gateway-unavailable assertion uses J-B without matching evidence, so that particular case does not independently isolate outage behavior. Fail-closed lookup is nevertheless implemented in decide and explicitly required by q Dispatch 30,46,50.
Model abstracts signatures, duplicate handling, physical actions and lease expiry to supplied contracts; no defect conclusion relies on those omissions.
